text:
Alex: heads-up — we started seeing a wave of GPU node boot failures after yesterday's KMS key policy update in ap-east-1 and eu-west-1. pods stuck in Pending with node provisioning errors.
Alex: sample from node-init log: 
```
2026-03-18T08:12:23Z ERROR kubelet: failed to decrypt kubelet bootstrap token: AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:ap-east-1:123456:key/abcd-ef01
```
Maria: that's not great. was the key policy change pushed by terraform or a console edit?
Sanjay: terraform apply by infra-team, the change added a service principal for lambda audits but I thought we scoped the node roles too. digging.
OpsBot: ALERT: 1919994321 - Autoscaler scaled up 12 -> 20 nodes in ap-east-1 at 08:14:17 due to pod pending; 5 node boot failures reported.
Emma: @Sanjay can you paste the tf diff? if the node role lost kms:Decrypt that would explain it.
Sanjay: tf diff shows we replaced the key policy block: removed explicit allow for role arn:aws:iam::123456:role/redwood-node-provisioner and instead added a conditional for CloudTrail. probably accidentally removed the node principal.
Maria: ok EVAC plan: can we re-add the principal back into the key policy as an immediate rollback? that should let kubelets finish bootstrap.
Kevin: approving rollback now, but need audit trail — we must record the exact change to CloudTrail and S3 for compliance. I'll trigger a quick CloudTrail lookup.
Kevin: CloudTrail event found: eventID=0a1b2c3d userIdentity=terraform-redwood@infra commit=git+sha:5f3a9; time=2026-03-18T08:09:02Z
Alex: rolling key policy back via console for ap-east-1 to restore node role grant. doing it now.
Alex: done. nodes are re-attempting boot. saw one node come Healthy at 08:27.
OpsBot: EVENT: KMS key policy revert performed by Alex at 2026-03-18T08:26:10Z
Maria: follow-ups: (1) add a tf test for key policy to ensure node role always present, (2) add canary deploy for key policy changes in a non-prod region before prod, (3) make node boot resilient to KMS Deny by caching bootstrap tokens.
Sanjay: will open infra ticket and add terraform guardrail. also propose creating an alias fallback: if kms:Decrypt fails, use legacy alias/secondary key for node bootstrap during rotation window.
Emma: also we lost ~3 spot GPU nodes to re-provision churn — cost hit. rough back-of-envelope: extra on-demand for 6 hours across ap-east-1 =~ $1.8k yesterday. tracking in cost center INF-OPS.
Maria: add audit log capture: export CloudTrail events for the KMS change to secure S3 bucket and mark as evidence for compliance reviewer.
Alex: added minimal remediation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/322 — reintroduce node principal, add acceptance test. please review.
Kevin: on long-term: we should add an automated policy linter in CI that refuses key policy diffs that remove principals referenced in `infra/roles/node-provisioner.tf`.
Sanjay: agree. assigning INF-678: "KMS key policy CI guard + canary rollout" — will include runbook for rollback and cost estimation formula for GPU churn.
Emma: small ops note: tighten firewall egress for node provisioning traffic? we had one case where nodes hit an internal proxy that returned 502 during retries.
Alex: thanks all — monitoring cluster health for the next 24h and will follow up in the ticket with logs and exact cost numbers. :white_check_mark:
Maria: :thumbsup: good catch and quick rollback.
